title: Touriga Nacional
description: Portugal's finest red grape: floral, dark and structured, at the heart of Port and the Douro's dry reds.
L: Describe Touriga Nacional's aromas and structure

Touriga Nacional is a black grape native to Portugal. It gives deep-coloured wines with intense aromas of violet, bergamot, blackberry and black cherry, often with rockrose, a wild herb of the Douro hills. Tannins are firm and ripe, acidity fresh. It's considered the country's finest red grape.

Touriga Nacional probably comes from the Dão, where it was once called Tourigo. Its small berries and thick skins concentrate colour, tannin and aroma. Its natural yields are low, often under 1 kg per vine, which once made growers reluctant to plant it. Clonal selection since the 1970s raised yields and helped it spread.
Which aroma is most typical of Touriga Nacional?
Violet is Touriga Nacional's signature, often with bergamot and dark fruit.

In the glass, look for deep purple colour and a strongly floral nose, like violets and citrus peel, with dark fruit. On the palate, firm, fine tannins and fresh acidity, with a long finish. In blends, it adds perfume and structure that you can often pick out.
Touriga Nacional naturally gives high yields.
Not true. Its yields are naturally low, which is part of why its wines are so concentrated.
Touriga Nacional gives violet, bergamot and dark fruit
It probably comes from the Dão and has naturally low yields
It's deep, floral and firm, Portugal's finest red
Name countries that have adopted it

Touriga Nacional is planted in most Portuguese regions, but the Douro and the Dão are its heartlands. In the hot, dry Douro, on schist, it gives powerful, concentrated wines. In the Dão, cooler and granite-based, it gives more elegant, floral wines with fresher acidity. It also grows in Alentejo, Lisboa and Bairrada.

Touriga Nacional handles heat and drought well thanks to deep roots and small berries. Strong sun develops its colour. In very hot sites it can lose some aromatic finesse, so higher or north-facing vineyards are valued. Its vigorous growth needs careful canopy management.
Match each Portuguese region to its Touriga style.
Portugal's regions bring out different sides of the grape.

With warmer summers, other countries are interested. Bordeaux approved Touriga Nacional for trial in its AOCs in 2021, as a heat-tolerant option. It also grows in Spain, Australia, South Africa, where it's used for fortified wines, and California.
Why did Bordeaux approve Touriga Nacional for trial in 2021?
It handles heat and drought well
Bordeaux is looking for grapes adapted to a warming climate.
The Douro and Dão are Touriga Nacional's heartlands
It handles heat and drought well
Bordeaux, Spain, Australia and South Africa grow it too
Explain Touriga Nacional's role in Port

Port is a blend of many grapes. Touriga Nacional brings colour, tannin, structure and its floral perfume, essential for Vintage Port, which must age for decades. It is usually a smaller share than Touriga Franca, the Douro's most planted grape, because of its lower yields. Most Port grapes are foot-trodden or machine-trodden in lagares.

Since the 1990s, the Douro has become famous for dry reds, often blends of Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca and Tinta Roriz. Barca Velha, first made in 1952, showed the potential. Today single-varietal Touriga Nacional from the Douro and Dão is common, often aged in French oak.
What does Touriga Nacional bring to Port?
Touriga Nacional is aromatic, not neutral.
Try a Douro dry red and a ruby Port side by side. The violet and dark fruit of Touriga Nacional link both, though one is dry and the other sweet.
Barca Velha, an early Douro dry red, was first made in ____.
1952. It showed that the Douro could make great dry reds.
Touriga Nacional gives Port colour, structure and perfume
The Douro now makes famous dry reds, since Barca Velha in 1952
Dry and sweet styles share its violet and dark fruit
Pair dry Touriga Nacional with food

Dry Touriga Nacional suits roast lamb, kid, game and Portuguese dishes like roast suckling pig from Bairrada or bacalhau with roasted potatoes. Its floral notes go well with herbs and its tannins with fat. Serve at 16 to 18 degrees, decanted when young.

Ruby and Vintage Ports suit dark chocolate, blue cheese like Stilton, and dried fruit. Serve Port slightly cool, about 16 degrees for ruby and vintage. Vintage Port needs decanting for sediment. Touriga Nacional's structure helps top Vintage Ports age 30 to 50 years.
Which is a classic partner for Vintage Port?
Salty blue cheese balances Port's sweetness and power.

Good dry Touriga Nacional from the Douro or Dão ages 10 to 20 years, gaining earthy, savoury notes while keeping its floral lift. Simpler versions are best young and fruity. Port's age depends on style: rubies are best young; vintages last decades.
Yes. It ages in bottle and throws a heavy sediment.
Dry Touriga Nacional suits lamb, kid and roast pork
Port suits blue cheese and dark chocolate
Good dry reds age 10 to 20 years; Vintage Port decades
